meta.title: Data Analytics Documents
meta.description: DDD documentation framework for Data Analytics. AI reads this file and generates .md files covering KPI definition, metric logic, data pipelines, dashboards, and governance.

agent_instructions.role: You are a data analytics documentation generator. Read this file and produce each document listed in phases[], in dependency order.
agent_instructions.generation_order_strategy: Topological sort by depends_on graph. Business-layer documents (KPI, Metric Spec) have no dependencies and are generated first. Visualization design spec bridges stakeholders and metrics into dashboard standards. Governance and AI docs are generated last.
agent_instructions.content_language: Write document content in Thai for narrative sections; use English for all identifiers, SQL, field names, table names, and technical terms.
agent_instructions.quality_gate: Each document must cover all sections[] listed. Validate that cross-references (refs[]) resolve to real document IDs before finishing. Metric definitions must be consistent across KPI Dictionary, Metric Spec, and Metric Logic. For each dashboard chart, verify chart type matches viz_design_spec.chart_type_matrix. If advanced viz (crosshair, animation) is used, confirm stakeholder data_literacy_level >= intermediate.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a DATA_MODEL_SPEC.md documenting the semantic layer. List all fact tables (e.g. fact_mrr_monthly, fact_usage_daily) and dimension tables (e.g. dim_customer, dim_product). For each table include: name, grain, key columns, description, and source system. agent_hints.input_context: Every metric in METRIC_SPEC.md must be traceable to at least one fact table. Grain defined in METRIC_SPEC.md must match the grain of the corresponding fact table.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a VIZ_DESIGN_SPEC.md that bridges stakeholder needs and metric shapes into concrete visualization standards. (1) Build a chart_type_matrix mapping each metric type (time-series ratio, categorical count, ranking, proportion) to a recommended chart type (line, bar, pie, table, heatmap) with anti-patterns and grain considerations. (2) Define a color_theme_spec with primary/secondary/accent palette, semantic colors (green=positive, red=alert, amber=warning), font rules — then produce a viz_theme.py code block exporting COLOR_PALETTE, FONT_RULES, and CHART_DEFAULTS as a reusable Python module; also output this as a standalone viz_theme.py file alongside the .md. (3) Define interaction_spec: tooltip format per chart type, crosshair behavior and cross-chart sync, click-through drill-down targets, animation rules. (4) Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios, colorblind-safe palette variant (protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia), screen reader alt-text and aria-label rules, keyboard navigation. (5) Data Literacy Guard Rails: map visualization complexity levels (basic=bar/line/table, intermediate=heatmap/scatter/crosshair, advanced=animated/multi-axis/custom) to each stakeholder group's data_literacy_level from STAKEHOLDERS.md — gate rule: never render a viz above the audience's literacy level.
agent_hints.input_context: Read STAKEHOLDERS.md for data_literacy_level per consumer group (basic/intermediate/advanced). Read METRIC_SPEC.md for metric types and grain. agent_hints.instruction: Generate a RUNBOOK.md as the on-call reference for the data team. For each common failure scenario include: trigger condition, severity (P0/P1/P2), first-response steps, root cause checklist, recovery procedure, and rollback steps. Scenarios must include: (1) pipeline fails to complete on schedule, (2) data freshness SLA breached, (3) metric value anomaly detected, (4) data quality check failure, (5) dashboard shows stale or missing data. Define escalation contacts and response time SLAs per severity. Include a post-incident review template.
agent_hints.input_context: Failure scenarios must reference PIPELINE_SPEC.md and SLA_FRESHNESS.md. Metric anomaly scenarios must reference DATA_QUALITY.md thresholds.
agent_hints.validation: Must cover at least 5 failure scenarios. Each scenario must have: trigger, severity, first_response_steps[], recovery_procedure, rollback_steps. Escalation contacts must include primary and secondary on-call. Response time SLAs must be specified per severity level.
